topic: Advanced Information Architecture and Complex User Flows
learningObjectives: Design information structures for complex applications.
Map multi-step user journeys and decision points.
Identify and reduce unnecessary complexity in navigation.

activities.title: Complex IA Explorer
activities.instruction: Explore how content is organized into categories, subcategories, and navigation levels.

content.concept: Complex information architecture organizes large amounts of content into understandable categories, levels, and navigation structures.
content.tip: Interact with each level to understand how information moves from broad categories to specific content.

items.label: Product Category
items.description: Groups related products into meaningful subcategories.

items.label: Product Detail
items.description: Provides detailed information about a selected product.

items.label: Checkout
items.description: Contains the steps required to complete a purchase.

items.label: Order Confirmation
items.description: Confirms that the user's transaction has been completed.

activities.title: Navigation Depth Lab
activities.instruction: Adjust the number of navigation levels and observe how the user's path changes.

content.concept: Excessive navigation depth can increase effort, while appropriate grouping helps users reach information efficiently.
content.tip: Compare shallow and deep structures and notice how many steps are required to reach the same content.

scenarios.description: Content is immediately available but may create crowded navigation.
Content is grouped into a moderate number of meaningful levels.
Users must pass through many levels before reaching content.

activities.title: Journey Flow Builder
activities.instruction: Build a multi-step journey containing actions, decisions, alternate paths, and completion states.

content.concept: Complex user journeys combine tasks, decisions, alternate paths, errors, and completion states.
content.tip: Connect the steps in a logical order and include an alternate path where a decision changes the journey.

activities.title: Flow Complexity Detector
activities.instruction: Identify the points where unnecessary complexity may create friction.

content.concept: Decision overload, unnecessary steps, unclear labels, and dead ends can make complex flows difficult to complete.
content.tip: Look for unnecessary decisions, repeated information, unclear actions, and paths that do not lead anywhere.

scenarios.question: A checkout requires users to choose between seven delivery options before they can continue.
scenarios.explanation: Too many choices at one point can increase cognitive effort.

scenarios.question: A user reaches a page where there is no action to continue or return.
scenarios.explanation: Users should have a clear way to continue, go back, or recover.

scenarios.question: A multi-step form asks for the same phone number on three different screens.
scenarios.explanation: Repeated input increases effort without adding user value.
